As for the ignorant, for whom guidance only increases them in error and clarity only increases them in blindness, the speech was not directed at them; and {it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe}.

{4} {A bringer of good tidings and a warner}; that is, a bringer of good tidings of reward, both immediate and deferred, and a warner of punishment, both immediate and deferred. He mentioned the details of both, and mentioned the causes and attributes through which good tidings and warning are attained. These attributes of the Book necessitate that it be received with acceptance, submission, faith and acting upon it. However, most of creation turned away from it, the turning away of the arrogant; {so they do not listen}: with the listening of acceptance and response, even though they may have heard it in a manner by which the legal proof is established against them.

{5} {And they said}; that is, these who turned away from it, making clear their non-benefit from it by closing the doors that lead to it: {Our hearts are in coverings}; that is, veils that are covered, {from what you call us to, and in our ears is deafness}; that is, a heaviness so that we do not hear you, {and between us and you is a barrier}: so that we do not see you. For this reason they said: {So act, indeed we are acting}; that is, just as you are content to act according to your religion, we are fully content to act according to our religion. This is among the greatest abandonment, for they were content with error over guidance, exchanged disbelief for faith, and sold the Hereafter for the world.

{6–7} {Say}: to them, O Prophet: {I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed}; that is, this is my attribute and my duty: that I am a human being like you, having no power over any matter, and I do not possess what you seek to hasten. God has only favoured me over you, distinguished me and singled me out with the revelation He revealed to me, and commanded me to follow it and to call you to it. {So take the straight path to Him}; that is, follow the path that leads to God, Exalted, by affirming the report He has given and following the command and avoiding the prohibition. {15} As for 'Ad, they, together with their disbelief in God, their denial of God's signs, and their disbelief in His messengers, were arrogant {in the earth}, dominating those around them among the people and wronging them. {25} That is: {And We appointed for them companions} — for these wrongdoers who deny the truth — {companions} from among the devils, as Allah the Exalted said: {Have you not seen that We sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with incitement?} That is, they urge them toward sins and stir them to them, because of what they adorned for them {of what was before them and what was behind them}. This is a question carrying the sense of a firmly established negation; that is, no one has a better word {ahsanu qawlan}, meaning a better speech, manner and state, than {the one who calls to Allah}: by teaching the ignorant, admonishing the heedless and those who turn away, and debating the people of falsehood; by commanding the worship of Allah in all its forms, urging it, beautifying it as much as possible, and warning against what Allah has forbidden, and making it ugly by every means that necessitates abandoning it. This especially applies to calling to the foundation of the religion of Islam and beautifying it, debating its enemies "in the way that is best," forbidding what opposes it of disbelief and polytheism, and enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong.

Among calling to Allah is making Him beloved to His servants, by mentioning the details of His blessings, the vastness of His generosity, the perfection of His mercy, and by mentioning the attributes of His perfection and the descriptions of His majesty.

Among calling to Allah is encouraging the acquisition of knowledge and guidance from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and urging that by every means that leads to it. Among this is urging noble character, doing good to all of creation, repaying the wrongdoer with kindness, and commanding the maintaining of kinship ties and kindness to parents. Among it is admonishing people in general at times of seasons, calamities and afflictions with what suits that situation, and other than that, whose instances cannot be counted, all of which fall under calling to all good and warning against all evil.

Then He, the Exalted, said: {And does righteous deeds} meaning: along with his calling the creation to Allah, he himself hastens to carry out the command of Allah by performing righteous deeds that please his Lord. {And says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"} meaning: those who submit to His command and follow His path. This rank is complete for the sincere (siddiqun) who strive to perfect themselves and perfect others, and who attain complete inheritance from the Messengers. Just as among the worst of people in speech are those who are callers to misguidance, following its paths. Between these two contrasting ranks, one of which rises to the highest of the high and the other descends to the lowest of the low, there are degrees that no one knows except Allah, and all of them are populated with creation. Each has degrees according to what they have done, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on surah 41, verses 34–35:

{34} He, exalted is He, says: ﴿The good deed and the evil deed are not equal.﴾ That is, the doing of good deeds and acts of obedience seeking the pleasure of God, and the doing of evil deeds and sins that anger Him and do not please Him, are not equal. Likewise, doing good to creatures and harming them are not equal, neither in their essence, nor in their description, nor in their recompense. ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ Then He commanded a particular kind of goodness that has great standing: doing good to one who has harmed you. So He said: ﴿Repel with that which is better.﴾ That is, if a person among the creatures harms you, especially one who has a great right over you, such as relatives, companions and the like, by word or by deed, then respond to him with goodness. If he cuts you off, then maintain ties with him; if he wrongs you, then pardon him; if he speaks ill of you in your absence or presence, then do not retaliate, but pardon him and deal with him in gentle speech; and if he shuns you and stops speaking to you, then speak kindly to him and offer him greetings. When you meet harm with goodness, a great benefit is achieved. ﴿Then, behold, he between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ That is, as though he were a compassionate close relative.

{35} ﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient.﴾ That is, none is enabled to this praiseworthy quality except those who restrain their souls from what they dislike and compel them to what God loves. Souls are naturally disposed to repaying the wrongdoer with his own wrong and not pardoning him, so how much more so to doing good. When a person restrains his soul, complies with the command of his Lord, recognizes the abundant reward, and knows that repaying the wrongdoer in kind does not benefit him and only increases enmity, and that doing good to him does not lower his standing, but whoever humbles himself before God, God raises him, then the matter becomes easy for him, and he does it with pleasure and sweetness. ﴿And none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ Because it is one of the qualities of the elect among creatures, through which the servant attains elevation in this world and the next, and it is among the greatest of the qualities of noble character.

Yet he does not thank God; rather he transgresses, exceeds the bounds, and says: ﴿This is mine﴾; that is, it came to me because I deserve it and am entitled to it. ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾; this is his denial of the Resurrection and his ingratitude for the blessing and mercy which God let him taste. ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I shall surely have the best with Him﴾; that is, supposing the Hour does come and I am returned to my Lord, I shall have the best with Him; just as the blessing came to me in this world, so it will come to me in the Hereafter! This is among the greatest audacity and speaking about God without knowledge. Therefore God threatened him with His saying: ﴿So We shall surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We shall surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾; that is, very severe.

{51} ﴿And when We bestow favour upon man﴾, with health, provision or other things, ﴿he turns away﴾ from his Lord and from thanking Him, ﴿and withdraws his side﴾; that is, he holds himself aloof out of arrogance and pride. ﴿But if evil touches him﴾, that is, sickness, poverty or otherwise, ﴿then he is one of lengthy supplication﴾; that is, very much, because of his lack of patience. For there is no patience in adversity nor thanks in ease, except for one whom God guides and graces.

{54} ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾; that is, they are in doubt about the resurrection and the Last Day, and they have no abode other than this worldly abode.
